newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World air cargo traffic up 5.1pct in Jan-Sept - AC.
newsitem.headline: World air cargo traffic up 5.1pct in Jan-Sept - AC.

text.p: Freight and mail handled by 477 airports around the world between January and September 1996, totalled 36.1 million tonnes, up 5.1 percent on the same period the previous year, said Geneva-based Airport Council International (ACI).
North America, the biggest ACI's six cargo-handling regions, reported 18.1 million tonnes of freight traffic, up 5.5 percent on January-September 1996.
Cargo traffic handled during the first eight months of the year at ACI's Europe member airports totalled 7,38 million tonnes, a rise of 3.8 percent on the same period in 1995.

Airports in the Asia/Pacific region (in which ACI incorporates Indo-China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan, Malaysia and Australia), handled 7.4 million tonnes, an increase of 4.7 percent on the first eight months of last year, ACI said.
Middle East airports recorded the highest growth rate of ACI's cargo-handling regions, rising 14.6 percent to 1.2 millon tonnes.
Latin American/Caribbean airport freight traffic was down 2.4 percent on 1995 levels at 821,097 tonnes.
Africa airports cargo traffic rose by 4.1 percent on the first eight months of 1995 to 314,184 tonnes. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 711 542 5017
